parts: Please review the brainstorm in papers/investigations-2/brainstorm, and also the investigations-2 README, and determine whether you agree with the next steps. Please add an additional file within the brainstorm folder discussing any changes you would make to the priorities.
I'll start by getting access to the repo on your computer and reading the project conventions.
The folder is connected now. Let me look at the investigations-2 folder on your machine.
I now have what I need. Let me record progress and write the review file.

The review is written and saved as `papers/investigations-2/brainstorm/PRIORITY_REVIEW_AFTER_AUDITS_CLAUDE_20261012.md` in your repo, with one link added to the README's reading map. Both changes are uncommitted; nothing else was touched. A copy is also in the project docs.

**Short version of the verdict.** I agree with the Codex brainstorm's three-part program and nearly all of its stop rules, and the arithmetic I checked in it is correct. I would change four things, one of them substantial:

1. **Priority 1 is aimed at the wrong artifact.** The brainstorm wants a specialist reconstruction package for the October 5 prose (the 11/12 strip). But at the very commit your audit pinned, `openai/math` marks the stronger September 30 theorem (7/8 for ζ, all Dirichlet L-functions, and the finite-order Hecke family over Q(√−3)) as formalized in Lean, with comparator statements I read directly: the ζ one is literally `riemannZeta s ≠ 0` for `7/8 < s.re` using Mathlib's own definition. Your repo knows the scope doc exists (the 8 Oct comparison note cites it) but says "No Lean proof was replayed" and still labels 7/8 an assumption. Since 7/8 implies 11/12, one `lake build` plus a careful reading of the bespoke Hecke statement outweighs any further prose audit as evidence for the *conclusion*. I made that priority 0, with the exact commands, module names, and the specific faithfulness checks the Hecke comparator needs. A third party reports a clean rebuild with standard axioms but did not build the Hecke module, which is the one your lanes actually use.
2. **Re-aim priority 1 at the mechanism.** The 11/12 moment sits exactly at the diagonal and beats Heath-Brown's general-coefficient cubic large sieve by `D^{(1−ϑ)/3}`, while Dunn–Radziwiłł (your own primary theta source) show that sieve is sharp under GRH. The specialist page that matters is the one naming where the Möbius/sextic structure is consumed. That page is also the gate for the small-cofactor probe (item 3).
3. **Newman:** audit `E_max` before Lemma 8.4 (it is 29% of the weakest certified row; the barrier has 400× slack), drop the full producer regeneration (order ten CPU-years), and put the Gordon/Planat method comparison *above* the sharp-lane screen, since 0.1745 is dominated by two public claims and the only thing worth learning is their lever.
4. Housekeeping: the merge markers the brainstorm mentions are already gone from your working tree; `DRAFT_HISTOR` vs `DRAFT_HISTORY` is inconsistent across projects.

Two things I could not do: arXiv:2610.12234 ("Slightly improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis") was refused by the fetch proxy, so it is flagged as must-read rather than summarized; and I did not compile any Lean.

Sources: [openai/math repository](https://github.com/openai/math), [Lean scope doc 003](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/lean/docs/003.md), [tomoto0 verification repo](https://github.com/tomoto0/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-7-8-verification), [arXiv:2610.12234](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12234v1), [Dunn–Radziwiłł abstract](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.07463), [expert-reaction summary](https://explainx.ai/blog/openai-math-results-that-matter-expert-reactions-2026), [emergentmind summary of result 003](https://www.emergentmind.com/openai-math-explorer/results/003).

parts: The arXiv paper you uploaded is directly relevant — it's Baiying Liu's 8 October improvement of the 7/8 bound, with its own Lean formalization. Let me read the parts that bear on your program.
Now let me write the revised file back to your repo (same path), update the README's one-line description, and refresh the project copy.

I read Liu's paper in full and revised the review file in place (same path in `brainstorm/`, README link text updated, project copy refreshed; still uncommitted). The paper changes one thing materially and sharpens two others.

**It supersedes your character-amplification lane.** Liu takes the September 30 geometry and varies exactly the two length parameters your lane varied: the summation-exponent difference `b` and the total selected prime length `ℓ`, with the same boundary formula `B = 11/12 − ℓ/4`. Your lane kept `b = 1/8` and took `ℓ = 1/6 + 1/6000` to get the conditional `7/8 − 1/24000`, and computed the limit of that family at `0.8749572006`. Liu's rational result uses `ℓ = 1/6 + 1/10000` (so your lane went further on that axis), and his algebraic result optimizes `b` too and lands at `B_new = 0.8749570698`, which is `1.3·10⁻⁷` below your lane's limit. He proves the three affine constraints force `B ≥ B_new`, states the expectation that it's optimal for the whole estimate system with `3/4 ≤ κ ≤ 1`, and reports a Lean 4 formalization with standard axioms. Your lane's proposed next target `7/8 − 1/20000` sits below his optimum, so his optimality remark says what your lane already said: a new estimate is needed, not a parameter. I recommend closing the lane with a dated note recording the parameter correspondence (your limit computation is a useful independent corroboration of his Lemma 19.1 and Proposition 25.1) and never reopening it for geometry, including the `κ` extension he estimates at `4.5·10⁻⁸`.

**It answers the mechanism question for the September 30 route.** His Part I and Appendix B are the theorem-to-application index the brainstorm wanted. The engine is one cubic-theta average evaluated two ways (reflection with the theta mean square from the quadratic large sieve, versus Poisson summation isolating the principal `1/L` term), a zero detector from two simultaneously large character polynomials, and two moments: the Möbius-weighted second moment proved by an inverse-moment induction with two finite Poisson transforms plus sixth-power amplification (Lemmas 17.1–17.6), and the unweighted fourth moment. That is the architecture your arithmetic audit reconstructed for the October 5 chain, so priority 1 becomes a crosswalk rather than a reconstruction package, and priority 0 should list which of those lemmas sit in the Hecke module's formal import closure.

**It confirms the 11/12 stage is load-bearing** in the 7/8 proof (the character count needs `δ ≤ κ ≤ 5/6`), which is worth knowing before anyone decides the October 5 route is idle.

One caveat I kept explicit: I did not open Liu's Lean repository, so his formalization claim carries the same "until replayed" label as OpenAI's.
